# A sensor network for Kandy: what to buy, where to put it, and what it would settle

**Drafted 2026-09-05.** Design generated by `scripts/design_sensor_network.py`; receptor layer by
`scripts/pull_kandy_receptors.py`. Candidate coordinates in
`data/processed/decomp/sensor_design_kandy.csv`.

---

## 1. What this campaign is for, and what it is not for

**It is not for building a validated one kilometre map.** This project has measured, six times,
that within-city spatial pattern is not recoverable from globally available covariates, once with
a detection limit fixed in advance. It has also measured that a tenfold refinement of the grid
moves the paired-site ratio by essentially nothing. A campaign sold as "we will now make the map
finer" would be spending money against a result this project already has.

**It is for four things the existing evidence says are worth measuring**, in descending order of
how well the evidence supports them:

1. **Anchoring the level.** Of four independent Kandy point records, three sit below the model
   and one matches, and the one that matches has an undocumented instrument. This is an open
   discrepancy on the axis the project calls strong, and one reference-grade instrument closes
   it.
2. **Measuring the within-cell distribution.** Chapter 8 argues this is the well-posed quantity,
   the larger of the two, and unreported by any gridded product. Nothing but paired microsites
   can measure it.
3. **Testing whether the spatial ceiling is a sampling artefact.** Every network scored so far is
   a convenience sample. This design deliberately is not one, which makes it an experiment.
4. **Establishing what susceptible people actually breathe**, which is a different question from
   what a map says and is answered at different locations.

---

## 2. The three measurements that determine the design

**The design space is enormous and the present network samples almost none of it.** Across the
15 by 15 km domain the fine emission surface spans **65 times** from its 10th to its 90th
percentile at 94 m resolution. The existing fixed records sit between the **61st and 100th
percentile** of that range. The entire lower 61 per cent is unsampled, and one of the two
low-cost sensors is **outside the domain altogether**. A network cannot recover a gradient it
never straddles, and this one never straddles it.

**The microscale signal is real, large and local.** A 25-site survey inside the city recorded
concentrations falling from 110 to 4 micrograms per cubic metre over 300 metres, with an
R-squared of 0.82 against traffic intensity. Two of its sites, 300 metres apart inside one model
cell, differ by a factor of 27.5 observationally while the model returns exactly unity. The
decay length is tens to hundreds of metres.

**Susceptible people are concentrated where the model is least trustworthy.** Of 150 mapped
schools, health facilities and care institutions in the domain, **78 (52 per cent) sit above the
90th percentile of the emission surface**, and the median school sits at the 91st. That is a
statement about a proxy rather than a measurement, which is exactly the point: the receptors are
where the model's least validated axis matters most.

---

## 3. The design: 30 sites in four strata

Strata are kept separate because they answer different questions, and because **a site used to
fit a model cannot honestly validate it.**

| stratum | n | instrument | purpose |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **A. Anchor** | 1 | reference-grade | calibrates everything else; settles the level discrepancy |
| **B. Design** | 12 | low-cost | spans the covariate space; the model-information stratum |
| **C. Paired** | 9 | low-cost | 3 triplets inside single cells; the within-cell distribution |
| **D. Receptor** | 8 | low-cost | schools and clinics; exposure, **held out of fitting** |

### A. The anchor, and why it is non-negotiable

One reference instrument at the city centre, at the joint maximum of population and emission
intensity, which is where low-cost units are least trustworthy and where the most people are.
Every other sensor in this design is calibrated against it.

**Without it the campaign is not interpretable.** Low-cost particulate sensors have no universal
calibration: response depends on humidity, aerosol composition, sensor age and the design of the
calibration itself. A network of 29 uncalibrated units measures 29 unknown offsets. This is also
the acquisition the project's own value-of-information work ranks first for Kandy, and the only
route to it is the regulatory agency.

### B. The design stratum, chosen by the covariate space rather than by convenience

Twelve sites selected by **conditioned Latin hypercube sampling** over emission intensity,
elevation, terrain confinement and population, so the network reproduces the domain's joint
distribution instead of clustering where access is easy. Sites are thinned to a 400 m minimum
separation, because two sensors 200 m apart in the same regime buy one sensor's worth of
information.

**The result straddles what the present network misses.** The design stratum spans the 0th to
99th percentile of emission intensity with a median at the 40th, and **8 of its 12 sites fall in
the lower 61 per cent that no existing record samples.**

### C. The paired stratum, which measures the quantity the map cannot report

Three triplets, each at the steepest local gradient in the fine emission surface: an anchor
member, one at 100 m and one at 300 m offset **along the gradient** rather than along a contour,
so the pair straddles the contrast instead of running parallel to it. All three members of each
triplet fall inside the same model cell, which is what makes them a within-cell test rather than
a between-cell one.

**This stratum has the largest expected effect in the whole design and the sharpest prediction.**
The model's own fine surface predicts a within-triplet contrast of only **1.4 to 1.6 times**.
The one Kandy observation that exists at this separation suggests **27.5 times**. If the
observation is right, the model's fine surface under-represents microscale contrast by more than
an order of magnitude, and the campaign will show it in its first month.

⚠ A pair sharing one coordinate is one point recorded twice. The project has already had to
withdraw one apparent pair for exactly this reason, so every offset here is a genuinely distinct
coordinate and the generating script asserts it.

### D. The receptor stratum, and why it is fenced off

Eight sites at named schools, health facilities and care institutions, thinned to 150 m so two
institutions on one street are not counted as two sites, and spread across receptor type so the
stratum is not simply the eight most exposed schools.

**These sites are held out of all model fitting.** They are chosen for who is present rather than
for what they would teach a model, so using them to fit would both waste their value as an
independent test and bias the model toward institutional locations. Their role is to answer
"what do children at this school actually breathe" and to serve as an honest out-of-sample check.

---

## 4. Instrumentation and the calibration protocol

**Co-locate before deploying and after recovering.** Every low-cost unit spends at least two
weeks alongside the reference instrument before it goes out and at least one week on return.
This gives a per-device calibration and, from the difference between the two, a measured drift
rate. Without the closing co-location the drift is unbounded and the record cannot be corrected
retrospectively.

**Rotate one unit through the anchor continuously.** A single unit permanently at the reference
site provides an ongoing transfer standard, so a network-wide drift can be distinguished from a
change in the air.

**Log humidity with every measurement.** Low-cost optical sensors respond to hygroscopic growth,
and Kandy is humid for much of the year. A record without co-located humidity cannot be corrected
for it.

**Record mounting height, inlet exposure and distance to the nearest road edge at every site**,
because these are the variables the eventual analysis will need and they cannot be recovered
later from a photograph.

---

## 5. Temporal design

**Minimum twelve months.** Kandy's concentration has a strong seasonal structure with a March
maximum and a mid-year minimum, and the transboundary contribution is seasonal rather than
chronic. A campaign shorter than a year measures one season and generalises it.

**Include the March inter-monsoon peak and the mid-year monsoon minimum**, which bracket the
range. If the budget forces a shorter campaign, run two three-month windows at those extremes
rather than six continuous months in between.

**Hourly resolution or finer.** The diurnal cycle is bimodal, with a morning peak near 07, an
evening peak near 18 to 19, and the daily minimum at midday rather than at night. Daily means
destroy exactly the structure that distinguishes local traffic from regional background.

---

## 6. What this design would settle, ranked by how well it would settle it

**Definitely.** The level discrepancy, which needs only the anchor and three months. The
within-cell distribution at three locations, which needs the paired stratum and one month. What
eight named institutions are exposed to, which needs the receptor stratum and a year.

**Probably.** Whether the spatial ceiling is a sampling artefact or an information limit. With
21 fitting sites deliberately spread across the covariate space, a rank correlation against
held-out sites can be computed and compared against the benchmark of 0.309 that a single free
raster achieves. ⚠ At 21 sites the detection limit is coarse and should be computed and
registered before the campaign, not after.

**Not at all.** Source apportionment, which needs filter sampling and chemical analysis rather
than optical particle counters. The chemistry work of 2026-09-05 bounds the locally emitted
primary share only between 9.1 and 48.3 per cent, and **nothing in this design narrows that
range.** A speciation campaign is a separate proposal and should be costed as one.

---

## 7. What would falsify the premise

The design assumes deliberate siting breaks a ceiling that convenience siting could not. That
assumption is testable and the campaign tests it.

**If a deliberately contrasted 21-site network still yields a rank correlation near 0.2 to 0.3**,
the information-limited reading is confirmed far more strongly than six convenience-sample nulls
could confirm it, and the field gains a genuinely bounded statement about what kilometre-scale
products can do. **That is a good outcome, and it should be registered as such in advance** so it
cannot later be presented as a failed campaign.

**If it rises materially**, the ceiling was a sampling artefact, and this project's six nulls
have to be reread as a statement about network design rather than about the atmosphere.

Both outcomes are worth the money. A design that can only succeed is not an experiment.

---

## 8. Sequencing, and what to do first

**Phase 0, no equipment.** Register the analysis: the benchmark, the detection limit at 21 sites,
and the decision rule, all before deployment. The project's own record is that a null without a
stated detection limit converts a limitation of the experiment into a claim about the world, and
it cost four months once already.

**Phase 1, the anchor alone.** Secure the reference instrument. It settles the level discrepancy
on its own and every later phase depends on it. This is a letter and an agreement rather than a
purchase, and it is the long-lead item.

**Phase 2, the paired stratum.** Nine units, three locations, one month. The cheapest stratum,
the largest expected effect, and it can run before the design stratum is sited.

**Phase 3, the design and receptor strata.** Twenty units for twelve months.

**Phase 4, mobile augmentation if funds remain.** One or two units rotated through additional
locations on a fixed schedule, which extends coverage without extending the fixed network. Note
that a rotating unit measures different places at different times, so it informs the spatial mean
and not the temporal correlation, and it still needs the anchor.

---

## 9. Risks, stated so they can be planned for

**Siting failure.** Every coordinate here is a design, not a siting decision. Some will have no
power, no secure mounting, or an obstructed inlet. **The rule when a site fails a ground visit is
to move to the nearest cell in the same covariate stratum**, not to the nearest convenient
building, because the latter reintroduces exactly the convenience sampling the design exists to
remove. The generating script can supply the next-best candidate per stratum.

**Loss and theft.** Assume attrition. A design that only works at 30 of 30 sites is fragile;
this one degrades gracefully because the strata are separable, and the paired stratum is the one
to protect first since it has the largest expected effect per unit.

**Calibration drift** is handled by the closing co-location, and a unit recovered without one
should have its later record flagged rather than corrected by assumption.

**Over-reading a short record.** A campaign that runs through one season and reports an annual
figure repeats an error this project has already documented in its own extension tier, where
every aggregate diagnostic passed while the episode tail was absent.

---

## 10. Honest limitations of this plan

The emission surface driving the design is a **proxy** built from road-network centrality, not a
measured source inventory, and the project has separately shown it misplaces sources that are
spatially decoupled from roads. **Kandy has such a source**: biomass burning is 14.1 per cent of
measured mass against traffic's 7.6 per cent, and it has no admissible remote proxy. A design
that stratifies on a traffic-derived surface will under-sample residential burning, and the
honest response is to add sites in residential areas on that ground rather than to pretend the
proxy covers it.

The receptor layer comes from OpenStreetMap, whose completeness varies and cannot be measured
from the data. **A missing school is invisible here.** The 150 receptors are a lower bound.

Outdoor workers are the most exposed group in the city and **are not in this design at all**,
because they have no fixed location. Reaching them requires personal or mobile sampling, which is
a different instrument and a different protocol. Their absence is a gap in the plan rather than a
judgement that they matter less.

And the design optimises what can be computed, which is coverage of a covariate space. It does
not optimise expected reduction in decision loss, which is what a formal value-of-information
placement would do and what the nearest published work in this area does. That would need a
stated decision problem, and this project has not specified one.
